title: A localized Gaussian-witness lower bound for fractional iterated area on uniform grids
author: Alec Kriebel
description: A localized Gaussian-witness proof of an explicit finite-grid lower bound for estimating fractional Brownian iterated area, with scope and prior work.
abstract_source: Complete original abstract from published paper.tex, visually matched to paper.pdf p.1. Exactly one source paragraph. Mathematical notation expressed in Unicode/plain text; source TeX preserved verbatim in abstract-source.tex. No sentence or qualification omitted.
abstract_original_tex: For two independent standard fractional Brownian motions with the same fixed Hurst parameter $H\in(1/4,1)$, we give a localized Gaussian-witness proof that every square-integrable estimator of the canonical iterated integral $X_T=\int_0^T B^1_s\,dB^2_s$, based on both complete uniform grids of $n$ observations on $[0,T]$, has root mean-square error at least $c_HT^{2H}n^{1/2-2H}$. The positive constant is explicit and depends only on $H$; the inequality holds for every $T>0$ and integer $n\ge1$, including nonlinear estimators. Smooth compactly supported covariance paths, a Fourier periodization upper Gram bound, and an exact deterministic area pairing provide the witness. The Brownian optimum and the smooth asymptotic rate are prior results. Fourier localization and Gaussian projection have established antecedents; historical theorem and method priority, full novelty, and worldwide current-open status remain unverified. The note uses canonical-area existence and sufficient $L^2$ convergence, without endorsing exact Euler-error coefficients of the pinned arXiv v1.
abstract: For two independent standard fractional Brownian motions with the same fixed Hurst parameter H ∈ (1/4,1), we give a localized Gaussian-witness proof that every square-integrable estimator of the canonical iterated integral X_T = ∫₀ᵀ B¹_s dB²_s, based on both complete uniform grids of n observations on [0,T], has root mean-square error at least c_H T^(2H)n^(1/2−2H). The positive constant is explicit and depends only on H; the inequality holds for every T > 0 and integer n ≥ 1, including nonlinear estimators. Smooth compactly supported covariance paths, a Fourier periodization upper Gram bound, and an exact deterministic area pairing provide the witness. The Brownian optimum and the smooth asymptotic rate are prior results. Fourier localization and Gaussian projection have established antecedents; historical theorem and method priority, full novelty, and worldwide current-open status remain unverified. The note uses canonical-area existence and sufficient L² convergence, without endorsing exact Euler-error coefficients of the pinned arXiv v1.
plain_language: This note asks how much information is lost when two fractional Brownian paths are observed only at equally spaced times. The quantity to estimate is an iterated integral: one path is integrated against changes in the other.

The paper gives a positive lower bound for the root mean-square error of every estimator using both sampled paths. It includes nonlinear estimators and the conditional expectation, which minimizes that error. For a fixed Hurst parameter H between 1/4 and 1, the bound is c_H T^(2H)n^(1/2−2H), where n counts observations on each component and c_H depends only on H.

The proof constructs Gaussian variables whose covariance paths vanish at every observation time. Their products are invisible to the observations but have a nonzero pairing with the iterated integral. Controlling the size of this witness turns that pairing into an error bound.

The exact Brownian optimum and the smooth-range asymptotic rate were known before this note. The paper presents an attributed witness argument and does not claim first priority or a new general method.
result: For independent standard fractional Brownian motions B¹ and B² with the same fixed H ∈ (1/4,1), let X_T be the canonical iterated integral ∫₀ᵀ B¹_s dB²_s. For T > 0, integer n ≥ 1, and every F ∈ L²(σ(Bⁱ_(jT/n): i=1,2; j=1,…,n)), Theorem 1 states ‖X_T−F‖₂ ≥ c_H T^(2H)n^(1/2−2H).
The explicit positive constant is c_H = 2πa/(D_H√(P̄_fP̄_g)), with a=4/45045 and D_H, P̄_f and P̄_g specified by finite integrals and bounds in equations (1)–(2) of the unchanged paper.
why_it_works: Two compactly supported polynomial covariance paths are placed inside each grid cell. They vanish at both ends, so joint Gaussianity makes the witness vector independent of both complete observation grids.

A Fourier periodization estimate bounds the witness variance by a quantity proportional to n. A finite-sum identity and established L² convergence identify its exact covariance with the iterated integral.
Cauchy–Schwarz then gives the stated lower bound. The proof uses an upper Gram bound and does not require independent cells or an increment lower bound in the rough regime.
limitations: The two components must be independent standard fractional Brownian motions with the same fixed Hurst parameter H ∈ (1/4,1). Both complete uniform grids, including the terminal observation T, are used.
The result is a lower inequality for each n and T. It does not assert a sharp constant, an exact normalized-error limit, a limiting law, or a constant uniform in H.
The endpoints H=1/4 and H=1 are excluded. No result for nonuniform or adaptive sampling, unequal Hurst parameters, or correlated components is asserted.

The target is the canonical iterated integral. The halved antisymmetric area differs by an observed endpoint product and has the same optimal conditional residual; the unhalved antisymmetric difference has twice that residual.

Canonical-area existence and its identification with the polygonal limit are established external inputs. The paper supplies a sufficient L² convergence argument and does not endorse exact Euler-error coefficients in the pinned NTU arXiv v1.

Historical theorem and method priority, full novelty, and worldwide current-open status remain unverified. In particular, the broader implications of incompletely accessible Dickinson and Jackowski method bodies have not been excluded.
This is an unrefereed preprint prepared with extensive AI assistance. Finite checks are supplementary evidence and do not formally certify the universal analytic result.

background.title: Andreas Neuenkirch, A conjecture on the optimal approximation of the fractional Lévy area (2012)
background.note: States the same iterated-integral and uniform-vector-observation lower-rate question; the historical conjecture does not certify present-day openness.

background.title: Andreas Neuenkirch, Samy Tindel and Jérémie Unterberger, Discretizing the fractional Lévy area (2010)
background.note: Provides the area-construction and polygonal-limit interfaces. The institutional journal-formatted version is distinct from the pinned arXiv v1.

background.title: Andreas Neuenkirch and Taras Shalaiko, The maximum rate of convergence for the approximation of the fractional Lévy area at a single point (2016)
background.note: Establishes the smooth H>1/2 asymptotic optimal rate; its inspected author text also records the exact Brownian optimum.

background.title: Dongsheng Wu and Yimin Xiao, Geometric Properties of Fractional Brownian Sheets
background.note: Its sectorial local-nondeterminism proof uses harmonizable Gaussian representations and localized Fourier bumps.

background.title: Yimin Xiao, Properties of local-nondeterminism of Gaussian and stable random fields and their applications (2006)
background.note: Gives spectral and Gaussian-projection antecedents for local nondeterminism.
